mutant.description: THREE mutants, each aimed at a different way this deliverable could be green and wrong. (1) THE SEEDED BREAKAGE (F27-AC4 leg 2): the REAL driver output from a live run, with one `SCENARIO ready TAB reporting` line removed, graded through the SAME verdictFor the graded test uses -- it mutates the SUBJECT'S INPUT rather than the subject, so the test's own rule is what decides. (2) THE SEEDED LITERAL (F27-AC5): a file containing `const PORT = '5181'`, written to scratch and scanned by the same function BEFORE the real folder is scanned. (3) THE SEEDED TYPE ERROR (F27-AC1): `const SEEDED_TYPE_ERROR: number = 'positive control'` in the new test file. PLUS THE NEGATIVE CONTROL THAT IS NOT A MUTANT BUT THE DEFECT'S OWN COORDINATE, EXERCISED: F27-AC3's ABSENT arm does not wait to observe a missing server -- it MEASURES a port closed and points a real child run at it, so 'what does this instrument do when the precondition is absent?' is answered by running that exact state. PLUS TWO INSTRUMENT DEFECTS FOUND IN THIS CELL'S OWN WORK, BY ITS OWN ASSERTIONS, BOTH OF WHICH WOULD HAVE READ GREEN-ENOUGH and are disclosed here rather than repaired-and-forgotten: (i) the first probe asked 127.0.0.1 and returned ECONNREFUSED against a server answering HTTP 200, because vite binds [::1] only here -- a FALSE ABSENT, which under this cell's own law skips a runnable criterion silently (row IRPT_FNTEND-W3-S17); (ii) the first ABSENT arm set process.env and spawned a child, which bun 1.3.9 does not propagate, so the child read the DEFAULT port while every assertion except the one NAMING the value it had set still passed (row IRPT_FNTEND-W3-S18). The discriminator that caught (ii), `expect(declared[0]).toContain(closedPort)`, is retained in the test for exactly that reason.
